subtopics.title: Cold War Arms Control Milestones
subtopics.summary: Arms control between the United States and the Soviet Union progressed through a series of talks and agreements. The SALT I round produced the Anti-Ballistic Missile (ABM) Treaty, which limited missile defence to preserve mutual vulnerability. Later instruments such as SALT II, START I, START II and SORT set quantitative limits or served as interim pacts, but several were never ratified or were later abandoned.
facts: SALT I (1969-1972) resulted in the Anti-Ballistic Missile (ABM) Treaty.
The ABM Treaty restricted deployment of missile defence systems to preserve mutual vulnerability.
SALT II (1972-1979) set quantitative limits on nuclear delivery systems, including long-range missiles and strategic bombers.
The United States never ratified SALT II, owing to Soviet military intervention in Afghanistan.
START I (1991) capped 6000 nuclear warheads, enforced inspections and expired in 2009.
START II (1993) aimed to reduce nuclear weapons to 3,500; Russia withdrew after the US exited the ABM Treaty.
SORT (2002), also known as the Moscow Treaty, was an interim agreement between the US and Russia.

subtopics.title: Nuclear Treaties and Control Regimes
subtopics.summary: Beyond the US-Russia pacts, a set of global treaties and voluntary export-control regimes aims to limit nuclear weapons and their spread. The NPT classifies states as nuclear-weapon or non-nuclear-weapon states, the CTBT seeks to end nuclear testing, and the TPNW bans nuclear weapons outright. Export regimes such as the Australia Group, the MTCR and the Wassenaar Arrangement coordinate controls on sensitive goods.
facts: Outer Space Treaty (1967) bans deployment of weapons of mass destruction in outer space; all nuclear-armed nations are signatories.
NPT (1968) aims to prevent nuclear spread and promote disarmament, and classifies nations as nuclear-weapon or non-nuclear-weapon states.
CTBT (1996) seeks to ban all nuclear weapon testing for civilian and military use.
CTBT is signed by 185 countries and ratified by 170, but remains non-operational as ratification by key nuclear-armed states is pending.
TPNW (2017) bans development, testing, possession and use of nuclear weapons.
Missile Technology Control Regime (1987) is an informal political understanding with 35 members.
Australia Group (1985) is an informal export control forum formed after chemical weapons use in the Iran-Iraq War.
Wassenaar Arrangement (1996) is a voluntary export control regime with 42 members.
